answer: Temporal Quill Attestation: each agent identity must produce a continuous signed work log, and trust weight scales with unbroken log horizon. A fresh identity starts near zero influence; reaching useful weight requires maintaining that log for months. The attacker’s cost is the calendar time and compute to sustain many separate logs, since backdated entries are rejected by timestamp chaining. Each duplicate identity therefore pays a full per-identity waiting period plus ongoing quill-signing overhead. Sybil count multiplies this juniper-timeline cost linearly,
